guide.title: Black Mountain, New Hampshire: a 1935 Jackson hill's co-op that wasn't
guide.intro: Black Mountain describes itself as serving skiers "since 1935," per its own "The Mountain" history page, which also states that its J-Bar -- originally installed as the "Shovel Handle" -- was "the first overhead cable lift in the country." The Fichera family took over ownership in 1995 and ran it for nearly three decades before a 2023-24 closure scare and a 2024-26 ownership saga that ended with the mountain in new hands.

sections.heading: A near-closure, a rescue, and a sale
sections.body: On October 13, 2023, the Fichera family announced Black Mountain would not open for the 2023-2024 season, citing "soaring energy costs, unpredictable weather, extreme staffing shortages throughout the region, and many other challenges," according to Boston.com. About a week later, on October 20, 2023, Indy Pass announced it would provide resources for the Fichera family to operate for one more season while a buyer was sought; Erik Mogensen -- founder of Indy Pass's parent company, Entabeni Systems -- said at the time, "We are not interested in owning ski resorts but are firmly committed to supporting independent operators like Black Mountain." On October 4, 2024, Entabeni Systems announced it had purchased Black Mountain's operating entity, calling itself the "temporary owner" for the upcoming season, per NH Business Review. Doug Fichera, who "grew up on the mountain since 1995," stayed on as director of mountain operations, and Andy Shepard was named director of community engagement under the new ownership.

sections.heading: A co-op plan, abandoned
sections.body: At the October 2024 sale announcement, Mogensen stated his goal was to "transfer the area to a cooperative model," and Boston.com reported the plan was for Black Mountain to become a community co-op by the start of the 2025-26 season, quoting him: "This place needs to be owned by the people that are in this room. Period." Looking back on that fundraising effort in his March 12, 2026 letter on Black Mountain's own site, Mogensen wrote that the planned community corporation had sold all 15 of its $250,000 Class A shares plus over one-third of its $25,000 Class B shares, with more than 2,600 people expressing interest in $5,000 Class C shares. In that same letter, Mogensen announced the co-op conversion was being abandoned: Entabeni Systems would instead remain "the long-term custodian and again 100% owner of Black Mountain," buying back all shareholder stock "at par to their original purchase price," and relocating operations to "New Hampshire and the Mount Washington Valley." On March 17, 2026, Boston.com reported that Entabeni's and Indy Pass's headquarters would move from Colorado to Jackson, N.H., and that Mogensen had purchased Black Mountain outright for a second time, intending to make it "a laboratory for solving the challenges facing independent ski areas." As of these March 2026 announcements, Black Mountain is owned outright by Mogensen through Entabeni Systems, the parent company of Indy Pass, not by a community co-op.

sections.heading: In Jackson
sections.body: Honeymoon Bridge, a wooden Paddleford Burr Truss covered bridge over the Ellis River, was built in 1876 and designed by Charles Austin Broughton and his son Frank, per Wikipedia. The Jackson Ski Touring Foundation (Jackson XC) operates a cross-country ski and snowshoe touring center offering instruction from PSIA-certified instructors and equipment rentals, and offers free season passes to children age 9 and younger, per its own website. The Wentworth, a Jackson Village hotel, traces to a property originally built by Trickey in 1869 as the Thorn Mountain House, which evolved during the 1880s into Wentworth Hall, per Wikipedia's "Jackson, New Hampshire" article.

faq.question: Is Black Mountain a co-op?
faq.answer: No. A 2024 plan to convert Black Mountain to a community cooperative by the 2025-26 season was abandoned in March 2026; owner Erik Mogensen instead bought the mountain outright for a second time through Entabeni Systems, Indy Pass's parent company, buying back all shareholder stock "at par to their original purchase price," per his own March 12, 2026 letter.

faq.question: Who owns Black Mountain?
faq.answer: Erik Mogensen, through Entabeni Systems, per Boston.com's reporting on the March 2026 sale; Mogensen also serves as managing director of Entabeni's pass program. The Fichera family, who owned Black Mountain from 1995 until a 2024 sale, remain involved: Doug Fichera serves as director of mountain operations, per NH Business Review.

places.name: Honeymoon Bridge
places.summary: An 1876 wooden covered bridge over the Ellis River in Jackson village.
places.history: Honeymoon Bridge, a wooden Paddleford Burr Truss covered bridge over the Ellis River in Jackson, NH, was built in 1876, according to Wikipedia's "Honeymoon Bridge (New Hampshire)" article. The bridge was designed and built by Charles Austin Broughton and his son Frank, per the same source.
